gaps.gap: The four previously-unread Vietnam legal sources (Baker McKenzie, Duane Morris, Conventus Law / 'companies-developing-and-using-ai-in-vietnam', Vietnam Briefing) have now been read in full by the corpus critic. This is NOT a fetch gap — it is a verification finding that must be carried into the draft, because it materially strengthens (and partially corrects) the jurisdictional conclusion in Tension 4 / promote-gate-efficacy. Key findings: (1) The Conventus Law source states the Vietnamese Law's Article 14 deployer obligations for HIGH-RISK AI systems include 'maintain the possibility of human intervention during use' -- this is the operative HITL-adjacent clause, and it is scoped to deployers of high-risk *deployed* systems, not to an internal prompt-management/versioning platform. (2) Decree 142/2026/ND-CP's medium-risk exemption criteria (already in the corpus, re-read) exempt systems that 'do not interact with or provide services or content directly to the public' -- an internal, non-public-facing prompt register plausibly falls to low-risk or outside the AI-system definition entirely, which is a stronger and more specific basis for the committed position than was available before. (3) The Law's passage date (10 Dec 2025) and effective date (1 March 2026), which comparisons.md flagged as 'uncorroborated in the two Vietnam sources read', is in fact independently corroborated by THREE more sources (OneTrust, Baker McKenzie, Duane Morris) -- the caution in comparisons.md should be relaxed to 'corroborated by four independent sources'. (4) The '12-18 months' transition figure the orchestrator originally passed down, which comparisons.md flagged as a probable confusion with the Decree's 60-day notification deadline, is ALSO independently real: Baker McKenzie and Duane Morris both state the LAW (not the Decree) grants '12 months for other AI systems' and '18 months for AI systems in health/education/finance' as grace periods for pre-existing systems. Two different, both-real provisions exist (a 12-18-month Law grace period AND a 60-day Decree notification deadline); the draft should state both rather than treating one as an error. (5) One residual, genuinely open question no source resolves: whether the prompt-management platform (or its improvement-agent component specifically) itself meets the Law's broad definition of 'AI system' ('machine-based system... makes inferences from inputted data to generate outputs'). This is a live interpretive gap, not a sourcing gap -- flag as an audited absence rather than search further; it would require actual MOST regulatory guidance or legal counsel opinion, not publicly available yet.
